about: The native matrix's declared departures (R3 as ruled, 1108; scripts/native-matrix/departures.mjs): the one place a judged row may differ from the vendor's and not fail. One kind of entry only: cua refused, or answered unconfirmed, where the vendor answered ok. Each entry names the row ({section, id}), both answers (vendor {answer: 'ok'}; cua {answer: 'refused' | 'unconfirmed', errorName: the engine's name for it, which must be one of that kind's (scripts/native-matrix/answers.mjs), sentence: a regular expression specific to the case's answer}) and the Decision Log entry that made cua conservative there (decision), and may say in a few words what the vendor does there (capability), which the report's known capability difference measures. The judge enforces the kind: an entry of any other kind, one naming a pressKey row (ruling 1119), an acceptance row (S L239), a refusal case, or a speed, finding or not-judged row, or one whose sentence is too broad, is itself a failure. A declaration covers a cua sample only beside the observed pair from an eligible run (one hold, commit and approved build), the vendor's ok, cua's recorded error name and sentence, with the row's own effect and interference checks on both sides; it never supplies an answer nobody observed. Everything else that differs fails, except a failure cua shares with its paired vendor sample (ruling 1144), which is listed apart as a shared limit.

cua.sentence: Google Chrome for Testing's web page does not accept a background click

departures.decision: Decision Log, 2026-11-05, #282 (shared mode, item 6): a drag into a background Chromium web area is never posted, refused as backgroundClickRefused; the background-drag study, #591 (ruling 1228)

acceptedMissesAbout: Ruling 1240: a speed op whose miss of the 10% beat the owner accepted (scripts/native-matrix/departures.mjs readAcceptedMisses). Each entry names the speed row ({section: 'speed', id}), its ticket and its ruling. The op stays judged and shown with its numbers; a miss it covers reads accepted, blocks nothing and is no owner's fork. An entry that names no speed row, or cites no ticket or ruling, is itself a failure. Ruling 1278: an entry's optional bound (the re-measurement it was accepted at: ruling, evidence, n, cua and vendor median and p95) holds the acceptance only while a re-measurement's cua/vendor median and p95 ratios are each at most the bound's; worse, the miss is the owner's again, with why (scripts/native-matrix/departures.mjs acceptanceExceeded).
